title: Cleartrip's Big Billion Days Sale: Flights From Rs 1,499, Hotels 40% Off
excerpt: Cleartrip's Big Billion Days 2026 travel festival runs October 8–18 with time-slotted deals across flights, hotels, buses and trains, plus bank discounts for HDFC cardholders.
body:
• Booking window: October 8 to October 18, 2026, on the Cleartrip app and website. Deals run in fixed daily time slots — Price Drop (12–2 pm), Tick Tock Deals (2–5 pm), Flash Sale (7–9 pm) and Last Minute Deals (10 pm–12 am) — plus a Rush Hour at the sale's opening.
  • Headline numbers: domestic flights from Rs 1,499 and international fares from Rs 5,999 (limited inventory); hotels at flat 40% off, with 4-star hotels at minimum 44% off in Tick Tock Deals; buses 15–20% off; trains up to Rs 180 off; BOGO hotel stays (code BOGO) on premium brands like Lemon Tree, Royal Orchid, Fern and Ginger.
  • Family offers: child flies free on domestic bookings of 2+ tickets during the Flash Sale, and flat 20% off international family bookings of 3+ passengers; Vande Bharat trains up to Rs 400 off in Last Minute Deals.
  • Stack your savings: HDFC Bank credit cards get a flat 10% off, and Cleartrip Elite members get minimum 20% off hotels plus flight date changes at Re 1. Check inventory caps and T&Cs — the lowest fares are marked limited inventory.

Cleartrip has kicked off its Big Billion Days 2026 travel festival, billing it as India's biggest travel sale, with the booking window running October 8 to October 18 and time-slotted deals across flights, hotels, buses, trains and holiday packages.

The Flipkart-owned travel platform is structuring the sale around fixed daily offer windows rather than a single flat discount. The day opens with a Price Drop slot (12 noon–2 pm) advertising domestic flight fares from Rs 1,499 and international fares from Rs 5,999 on limited inventory, hotels at a flat 40% off, buses 15% off, trains up to Rs 150 off — and a free partner visa for Vietnam and Bali. Tick Tock Deals (2–5 pm) push 4-star hotels to a minimum 44% off, with buy-one-get-one-free offers on buses and trains in narrow one-hour windows. The evening Flash Sale (7–9 pm) targets families: a child flies free on domestic bookings of two or more tickets, international family bookings of three or more passengers get a flat 20% off, and premium hotel brands go buy-one-get-one (code BOGO) with minimum 20% off. Late-night Last Minute Deals (10 pm–12 am) cover luxury hotels at minimum 10% off, Volvo buses up to Rs 400 off and Vande Bharat trains up to Rs 400 off.

Context & Background

The travel festival lands in the middle of India's festive sale season. Flipkart's flagship Big Billion Days runs alongside, and Myntra's Big Fashion Festival went live on October 8 with a claimed 8 million-plus styles, according to YourStory. Cleartrip, a Flipkart group company, announced its travel festival on October 7, framing the sale around the festive-season travel urge — trips home to visit family, and vacations timed to the holidays.

"No trip should be postponed simply because the timing didn't feel right or the price didn't add up."

— Manjari Singhal, Chief Growth and Business Officer, Cleartrip

Cleartrip is also pushing its Elite membership during the sale, promising members a minimum 20% off hotel bookings and flight date changes at Re 1, with a flat 10% off for payments made with HDFC Bank credit cards. All advertised discounts carry asterisks — limited inventory on the lowest fares, and terms and conditions on the BOGO and family offers.

Impact & Analysis

The timing is deliberate. October–November is peak domestic travel season in India, with Diwali falling in the booking window's wake and flight and hotel prices typically climbing through the festive period. A sale that front-loads the cheapest inventory into narrow daily windows is designed to do two things: pull forward bookings before the festive price surge, and keep shoppers returning to the app multiple times a day.

For travellers, the real value sits in the stacked offers rather than the headline fares — the Rs 1,499 domestic fares are explicitly limited inventory and will go first, while the combinable bank discount and Elite membership perks apply more broadly. The family-travel offers (child flies free, 20% off international family bookings) are the standout for festive-season trips home.

Diaspora Angle

For NRIs planning trips to India around Diwali and the winter holidays, the October 8–18 window is well timed: international fares from Rs 5,999 (limited inventory) and 20% off international family bookings of three or more passengers apply to inbound legs, and the hotel discounts cover the stays once you land. Book early in the window — the cheapest inventory is capped.

What's Next

The sale runs through October 18. Watch the daily time slots: the lowest fares and BOGO windows are the first to sell through, and the Rush Hour deals at the sale's opening hours set the pattern for each day's inventory drops. As with every festive sale, read the fare rules before paying — the cheapest tickets are typically the least flexible.
